newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand raises bank rate to 12.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand raises bank rate to 12.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Wednesday it was raising its key bank rate to 12.5 percent from 10.5 percent, effective immediately.
The bank rate is the rate the central bank charges on loans to commercial banks.

Analysts said the central bank raised its bank, or discount rate, to reflect higher inflation and higher domestic interest rates that would likely result from the Thai decision to let its baht float. The rate was last changed in 1995.
The rate increase comes along with an announcement by the Bank of Thailand and the Ministry of Finance that the Thai exchange rate system would be a managed float, effective on Wednesday.

The statement issued by financial authorities did not give many details about the exact way in which the managed float would work, but said the value of the baht would be determined by market forces to reflect fundamental economic forces.
Since 1984 the baht had been set against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
